engines.title: Anisotropic slab waveguide
engines.description: Guided TE/TM modes of a uniaxial film (x-, y- or z-cut, principal propagation axis) between isotropic cladding layers; arbitrary anisotropic stacks via slab_modes in Python.
references: A. Yariv and P. Yeh, Optical Waves in Crystals (Wiley, 1984), ch. 11
K. Okamoto, Fundamentals of Optical Waveguides, 2nd ed. (Academic Press, 2006), ch. 2

neff_uniaxial_film.title: Uniaxial film on isotropic substrate
equations: TM: kx² = k0² n_p² - β² n_p²/n_n²
TE: E_y, E_y' continuous; TM: H_y, H_y'/n_p² continuous

inputs.name: n_e
inputs.label: Extraordinary index n_e (optic axis = crystal z)

inputs.name: cut
inputs.label: Cut (crystal axis along the surface normal)

outputs.name: n_trans
outputs.label: Film index along the transverse axis

engines.title: Multipass-cell billiard path statistics
engines.description: 2D ray tracing of stadium and segmented-polygon multipass cells with input and output ports; transmission, mean path and gas-equivalent path, Monte Carlo or ergodic mean field.
references: L. A. Bunimovich, Commun. Math. Phys. 65, 295 (1979) (stadium billiard)
N. Chernov, J. Stat. Phys. 88, 1 (1997) (mean free path πA/P of planar billiards)

inputs.name: curvature
inputs.label: Polygon facet curvature 1/ρ (+ convex into the cell)

outputs.name: trapped_fraction
outputs.label: Rays still trapped at the end

engines.title: Bragg grating
engines.description: Coupling coefficient, peak reflectance, bandwidth and exact stack reflectance of a Bragg grating; oblique-incidence (s/p, TIR) stacks and etched-trench membrane DBRs.
references: H. Kogelnik, in Guided-Wave Optoelectronics, ed. T. Tamir (Springer, 1988)
M. Born and E. Wolf, Principles of Optics, §1.6 (characteristic matrices)
H. A. Macleod, Thin-Film Optical Filters, 4th ed. (CRC, 2010), ch. 2 (tilted admittances)

coupling_coefficient.title: Coupling coefficient κ
equations: κ = 2 Δn sin(π m f) / (m λ)

grating_summary.title: Peak reflectance and bandwidth
equations: Δλ_null = λ^2 / (π n_g L) sqrt((κL)^2 + π^2)

stack_reflectance.title: Quarter-wave or arbitrary periodic stack
equations: M = [[cos δ, -i sin δ / n], [-i n sin δ, cos δ]]

oblique_reflectance.title: Stack at oblique incidence (s/p, TIR)
equations: η_s = n cos θ, η_p = n / cos θ
M = [[cos δ, -i sin δ / η], [-i η sin δ, cos δ]], δ = k n d cos θ

inputs.name: sin_incidence
inputs.label: sin θ in the input medium

engines.title: Gaussian beam
engines.description: TEM00 beam radius, curvature, Gouy phase, Rayleigh range and thin-lens focusing.
references: A. E. Siegman, Lasers (University Science Books, 1986), ch. 17 and 20

engines.title: Material refractive index
engines.description: Sellmeier phase index, group index and GVD of SiO2, Si3N4, Si, LiNbO3, LiTaO3, KTP (x, y, z), BBO, AlN, GaAs, TiO2 and sapphire; temperature-dependent index of MgO:LiNbO3.
references: I. H. Malitson, JOSA 55, 1205 (1965)
D. E. Zelmon, D. L. Small, D. Jundt, JOSA B 14, 3319 (1997)
K. Luke et al., Opt. Lett. 40, 4823 (2015)
O. Gayer, Z. Sacks, E. Galun, A. Arie, Appl. Phys. B 91, 343 (2008)
K. Kato and E. Takaoka, Appl. Opt. 41, 5040 (2002)
D. Zhang, Y. Kong, J.-Y. Zhang, Opt. Commun. 184, 485 (2000)
T. Skauli et al., J. Appl. Phys. 94, 6447 (2003)
J. Pastrnak and L. Roskovcova, Phys. Stat. Sol. 14, K5 (1966)
J. R. Devore, JOSA 41, 416 (1951)
W. L. Bond, J. Appl. Phys. 36, 1674 (1965)

refractive_index.title: Phase index, group index and GVD
equations: n^2 = 1 + sum_i A_i λ^2 / (λ^2 - B_i)  (or the published form of each fit)

engines.title: Membrane slab mode for evanescent sensing
engines.description: Effective and group index, evanescent absorption factor Γ, penetration depth and surface-field weight of a free-standing membrane slab mode; evanescent gas volume.
references: A. W. Snyder and J. D. Love, Optical Waveguide Theory (Chapman and Hall, 1983), ch. 11-12 (slab modes, power and absorption integrals)
G. Stewart, B. Culshaw, Opt. Quantum Electron. 26, S249 (1994) (evanescent-wave absorption factor)
F. P. Payne, J. P. R. Lacey, Opt. Quantum Electron. 26, 977 (1994) (sidewall-roughness scattering ∝ surface field)

evanescent_mode.title: Evanescent absorption factor Γ
equations: TM: Γ = n_c ∫_clad (β²H² + H'²)/n_c⁴ / (k β ∫ H²/n²)

engines.title: Multipath interference (speckle) noise
engines.description: Random-phase path model of interference noise in multipass cells; thermal pattern shift, two-path coherence and equal-path contrast as calculator functions (the full model works on billiard_cell ray tables).
references: J. W. Goodman, Speckle Phenomena in Optics (Roberts, 2007), ch. 3 and 5 (random phasor sums, polychromatic speckle)
J. A. Silver, Appl. Opt. 44, 6545 (2005) (etalon fringes in multipass cells)

thermal_shift.title: Thermal shift of the fringe pattern

pair_coherence.title: Two-path visibility (Lorentzian source)
equations: V = exp(-2π Δν n_g ΔL / c)

engines.title: Three-wave phase matching
engines.description: Phase mismatch, QPM period of any order, coherence length and sinc² response for ω3 = ω1 + ω2 with arbitrary mode indices (bulk, birefringent or modal).
references: M. M. Fejer, G. A. Magel, D. H. Jundt, R. L. Byer, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. 28, 2631 (1992)
R. W. Boyd, Nonlinear Optics, 3rd ed. (Academic Press, 2008), ch. 2

engines.title: QPM second-harmonic generation
engines.description: Phase mismatch, first-order poling period, coherence length and QPM bandwidth for SHG.
references: M. M. Fejer, G. A. Magel, D. H. Jundt, R. L. Byer, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. 28, 2631 (1992)

engines.title: Ray phase vs launch angle in a multipass cell
engines.description: Optical path and phase of rays launched at slightly different angles into a segmented cell, pass by pass, and the fringe visibility left under launch-angle dithering.
references: J. W. Goodman, Statistical Optics, 2nd ed. (Wiley, 2015), ch. 5 (time-averaged interference, fringe visibility)
J. Reid, M. El-Sherbiny, B. K. Garside, E. A. Ballik, Appl. Opt. 19, 3349 (1980) (fringe suppression by modulation in tunable-diode-laser absorption)

first_mirror_phase.title: Phase to the first mirror vs angle

dither_visibility.title: Fringe visibility under angle dither
equations: linear phase: sine dither V = |J₀(aA)|, triangle V = |sinc(aA)|

outputs.name: phase_span_last
outputs.label: Phase span at the chosen pass

engines.title: Slab waveguide modes
engines.description: Effective index, V and b of a three-layer slab mode (multilayer stacks via multilayer_neff in Python).
references: K. Okamoto, Fundamentals of Optical Waveguides, 2nd ed. (Academic Press, 2006), ch. 2

slab_neff.title: Three-layer slab mode
equations: k d sqrt(n_f^2 - N^2) = m pi + atan(r_s γ_s / κ) + atan(r_c γ_c / κ)

engines.title: Step-index fibre LP01 mode
engines.description: LP01 effective index, V number and mode-field radius of a silica step-index fibre.
references: D. Gloge, Appl. Opt. 10, 2252 (1971)
D. Marcuse, Bell Syst. Tech. J. 56, 703 (1977)

lp01.title: LP01 mode
equations: U J1(U)/J0(U) = W K1(W)/K0(W), U² + W² = V²

engines.title: Trace-gas absorption lines
engines.description: Voigt line centre, widths, peak absorption coefficient and absorbance of trace gases near 1.5-1.7 µm (illustrative line list unless a HITRAN export is supplied); shot-noise-limited absorbance.
references: I. E. Gordon et al., J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf. 277, 107949 (2022) (HITRAN2020; line-strength and broadening conventions)
R. V. Kochanov et al., J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf. 177, 15 (2016) (HAPI)
J. Humlíček, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf. 27, 437 (1982) (Voigt via the Faddeeva function)

line_peak.title: Strongest line of a species
equations: γ_D = ν₀ sqrt(2 ln2 kT / m c²)
α = S N x V(ν - ν₀; γ_L, γ_D)

shot_noise.title: Shot-noise-limited absorbance
equations: σ_A = sqrt(2 q B / (ℜ P_in T_det))
